extracted.intended_audience: members of the Royal Society; natural philosophers, physicians, anatomists, astronomers, and natural historians
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and preparing natural-philosophy reports (anatomy, meteorology, ornithology, astronomy, medical case accounts) according to empirical, methodological, and descriptive standards exemplified in 17th‑century Royal Society communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of a disease account
rubrics_metrics.description: In treating of any disease, this author notices, 1. The history of the distemper. 2. The part affected. 3. The causes. 4. The prognostics. 5. The method of cure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clinical or pathological report should explicitly record the history, anatomical site, etiological factors, prognostic signs, and the therapeutic method; the work may be divided into parts and include surgical (Chirurgia Medica) and consultatory appendices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish animal vs vital faculties in pathology
rubrics_metrics.description: He looks upon it to be of the greatest consequence to distinguish between the animal faculty, placed in the spirits and genus nervosum, and the vital, whose seat is in the blood and viscera.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagnostic and pathogenic reasoning should separate nervous ('animal') functions from 'vital' (blood/viscera) functions, because causes, prognosis and treatments rest on this distinction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anatomical description must link structure to function
rubrics_metrics.description: After the anatomy of the brain, he discourses on the office of the brain and its parts, ... he gives likewise their use, founded on their structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anatomical accounts should not be mere inventories of parts; authors should propose functions inferred from structure and provide explanatory discussion connecting anatomy to presumed physiological role.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer human dissections for human anatomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Many of his predecessors ... had been content with dissections of the quadruped race; but this anatomist justly conceived that in different animals the structure of these parts must vary considerably, and therefore that an accurate knowledge of them, in relation to ourselves, was only to be acquired by dissections of the human subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the goal is knowledge about human anatomy and function, base descriptions and plates on human dissections rather than extrapolating from non-human species.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use plates/illustrations to accompany anatomical and descriptive works
rubrics_metrics.description: The work is illustrated by plates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishers/authors should include figures/plates to clarify anatomical structures and antiquities; illustrations serve as essential evidence and aid comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method for settling disputes between observational techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: A difference of this nature was not to be determined by conjectural speculations ... but by practical experience, and trials actually made both ways; and these duly examined and compared by persons competent to judge of such matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To adjudicate methodological disputes (e.g., telescopic vs plain sights), run side‑by‑side practical trials, have competent independent examiners witness and compare results, and base conclusions on empirical comparison rather than theory alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prescribed comparative test observations (astronomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author had often and earnestly desired that Mr. Hook would vouchsafe to give him at least these 8 distances, observed by his instruments ... to be compared with the same observed by this author: viz. 1. Lucidae Arietis a Palilicio; 2. Hujus k Polluce; 3. Pollucis a Regulo; 4. Reguli a Spica Virginis; 5. Hujusque k superiori in manu Serpentarii; 6. Hujus ab Aquila; 7. Hujusque k Marcab; 8. Atque hujus demum Lucida Arietis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When comparing observational setups, identify specific celestial distances/targets to be measured by each method so direct numeric comparisons can be made; publish the chosen test targets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeatability and precision as criteria of observational accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: He ... took, with his large brass sextant, the distance of Regulus and Spica; which he found to be 54° 1' 55", the same exactly, even to seconds, which he had six times before observed ... Many more observations were made from day to day ... most accurately, and almost incredibly to agree; and never to differ more than by an inconsiderable part of a minute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess accuracy by repeated measurements showing agreement to fine angular units (seconds or parts of a minute); repeated concordant observations are strong evidence of method reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent attestation and witness evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: He had from Bulliald, Buratin, Fullen, and others, who had been eye-witnesses of his observations, and assistant at them, great attestations of their accuracy ... Mr. Halley ... thought fit to leave in writing his attestation thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure written attestations from independent, competent observers who witnessed the experiments/observations; such attestations strengthen claims about precision and method validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish full data and observational lists for scrutiny
rubrics_metrics.description: He therefore gives, first, his observations of the year 1679 ... And therein, among others, the transit of some stars, and the occultation of some others ... From thence, to June 18, is an account of all his observations made with Mr. Halley, with their success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To enable verification and comparison, publish complete observation lists (dates, targets, instruments, results) and accounts of trials performed with other experimenters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ornithological species account content
rubrics_metrics.description: I send you an abstract of my notes about birds, which may be added ... Rubeculae excrementa semper liquida sunt ... intestinis caecis caret, aut ea valde exigua ... transmigrationis autem causa ex victu pretenda est. Nam ... ventriculos dissecui, in quibus maximam partem scarabaeos ... inveni ... Anserum ferorum 5 genera ... Caput ex fusco nigricat ... Pendet libras 7, et fere dimidium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Species accounts should include: feces/excrement characteristics, intestinal anatomy, diet evidence from stomach/ventricle dissections, migration timing and hypothesized cause (e.g., food availability), physical description (plumage, bill, legs), measurements (weight), habit and nesting data, and locality observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meteorological explanation should tie observed patterns to mechanism and topography
rubrics_metrics.description: These continual easterly winds between the tropics, I suppose, proceed both from the motion of the earth and the vertical influences of the sun ... the portion of the atmosphere under the line being extremely rarefied ... pressed westward ... the easterly winds between the tropics ... for the one half of the year ... they come from the south-east ... and for the other half ... from the north-east ... And hence it is that ... those who sail from China ... must wait for the northerly monsoon ... The causes of rain ... there is also requisite either a sudden change of winds, or a ridge of hills to meet the current of the air and vapours, whereby the particles of the vapours may be driven together, and so fall down in rain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts of winds/monsoons should combine observational evidence (ship routes, prevailing wind directions, seasonal shifts) with mechanistic explanation (earth rotation, solar heating/position, atmospheric density differences) and consider orographic/topographic effects (hills/ridges causing precipitation). Use navigation and regional examples to support claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use dissection evidence to infer behavior (migration) and diet
rubrics_metrics.description: Transmigrationis autem causa ex victu pretenda est. Nam tum temporis aves quoddam cibi genus ibidem reperiendum appetunt; ut autem id certo scirem, plurium ventriculos dissecui, in quibus maximam partem scarabaeos ... inveni.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer migratory behavior and dietary causes from direct anatomical/contents evidence (stomach/ventricle dissections) rather than conjecture; report such dissections as part of species natural history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualize published work by recording provenance and preservation
rubrics_metrics.description: This accurate astronomer laments the great calamity he suffered by fire ... he had, the same year, finished and published the latter part of his Machina Coelestis ... some of his papers, particularly his new catalogue of the fixed stars, were wonderfully preserved from the fire ... and he ... thought fit in the first place ... to publish these, for the satisfaction of others, to preserve the just reputation of his observations before published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When publishing observational/corporal work, document provenance, preservation status, and efforts to preserve or republish data; explain circumstances (loss, rescue of papers) that affect the corpus of evidence and availability for peer scrutiny.
